court: In the High Court of Madras†
appellants: Arulmigu Pidari Sri Anaiyalathamman Sangilikaruppu Temple, through its Hereditary Trustee, R. Meenakshisundari
case_number: W.P(MD) No. 10240 of 2026 and W.M.P(MD) No. 8044 of 2026
advocates: For R 1 & R 2 : Mr. M. Sarangan Additional Government Pleader
judgment_text:
Writ Petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, praying to issue a writ of mandamus, directing the respondents to permit the petitioner to administer the temple and to conduct all poojas and customary rituals including the temple festival and further direct the respondents to remove or keep in abeyance the operation of the illegally installed Hundial in the premises of Arulmigu Pidari Sri Anailyalathamman Sangilikaruppu Temple, which is situated within the compound of Kamatchi Amman Temple, Koothur Village, Pitchandar Koil, Manachanallur Taluk, Tiruchirapalli District, pending disposal of the statutory appeal before the Commissioner, HR&CE.

The Order of the Court was delivered by

D. Bharatha Chakravarthy, J.:— This writ petition has been filed for a mandamus permitting the petitioner to administer the temple and to conduct all poojas and customary rituals including the temple festival and further direct the respondents to remove or keep in abeyance the operation of the illegally installed Hundial in the premises of Arulmigu Pidari, Sri Anailyalathamman Sangilikaruppu Temple, which is situated within the compound of Kamatchi Amman Temple, Koothur Village, Pitchandar Koil, Manachanallur Taluk, Tiruchirapalli District, pending disposal of these statutory appeal before the Commissioner.

2. Upon hearing the learned counsel for the petitioner and perusing the material records of the case, it can be seen that the petitioner is claiming to be the hereditary trustee having certain exclusive rights even with reference to the temple. Earlier when the petitioner filed W.P(MD) No. 3981 of 2020, by an order dated 10-10-2022, this court directed the application filed by the petitioner under Section 63(b) of the Act and Status quo as on that date be maintained till the decision. Subsequently, it is seen that the said application ultimately came to be dismissed and the petitioner has now filed an appeal before the Commissioner, HR&CE.

3. It is stated by the learned Additional Government Pleader that the appeal was returned since it was beyond the period of limitation.

4. The learned counsel appearing on behalf of the third respondent would submit that he is also party in the Section 63 proceedings and he is not impleaded in the present writ petition.

5. Upon considering the submissions made by the learned counsel that the appeal has to be decided to determine the rights of the petitioner and in the meanwhile, if public offerings are made in the Hundial, the entire nature of the temple itself would be deemed to be changed, I am of the view that the relief can be granted to the parties in the following manner:

(i) Within two weeks from the date of receipt of the web copy of the order, the petitioner shall re-present the appeal.

(ii) Upon re-presentation thereof, the appeal shall be treated as one file within time and the same shall be dealt with on its own merits and in accordance with law.

(iii) Let the appeal be disposed of as expeditiously as possible in any event not later than five months therefrom. In the meanwhile, the installed Hundial need not be removed and otherwise can be made, but it can be opened only upon the final order that is passed by the Commissioner. No equitable rights can be claimed or the rights of the petitioner will be affected merely on the installation of the Hundial.

(iv) In the meanwhile, the petitioner will also be entitled to participate in the festival and no special honours to any person can be granted.

(v) With reference to the eviction proceedings relating to the temple properties, the same shall proceed irrespective of these proceedings.

(vi) No costs. Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
